title_en: Guzishta Lucknow (Lucknow of the Past: The Last Example of Eastern Civilisation in India)
author: Abdul Halim Sharar
first_published: serialised in Dilgudaz from 1913; first issued as a book in the 1920s
edition: Digital Library of India undated reprint; the last four pages (pp. 437-440, author's text only) are completed from the Maktaba Jamia edition of 1971. One leaf (pp. 203-204) is missing from the scan.
description: Abdul Halim Sharar's Guzishta Lucknow is the classic portrait of nineteenth-century Lucknow, the city in which, as Sharar puts it, the old culture of Muslim India made its last stand. Sharar (1860–1926), novelist, journalist and editor of Dilgudaz, grew up partly at Wajid Ali Shah's court in exile at Matiya Burj. After a short history of the Nawabs and Kings of Awadh, he describes the city's culture subject by subject: poetry, prose and speech; learning, medicine and calligraphy; martial arts and animal fights; music, dance and soz-khwani; food, dress and jewellery; houses, manners and conversation; the ceremonies of birth, marriage and death; the huqqa and pan; conveyances; and pottery. A basic source for historians of Awadh, Urdu, Hindustani music and everyday life. Complete Urdu text in 54 sections from the Digital Library of India copy, completed from the 1971 Maktaba Jamia edition, with a facing English translation, introduction and glossary.
translation_note: Faithful English translation made for this library, section by section, with translator's notes marked [TN]. Each reading section is one chapter, ending with a glossary.
